claim: Merged guidance asks contributors to reuse the existing PR for the same change.
limits_and_alternatives: The scope is duplicate PRs for one change, not several unrelated contributions. Integration is documented; universal compliance is not.

claim: The added guidance offers allowing maintainer edits and asking for help as an alternative when Git workflows cause problems.
limits_and_alternatives: Optional workflow support does not impose a duty to grant access.

claim: The discussion gives an assistance and workload rationale for the help option.
limits_and_alternatives: Attributed rationale is not a measured reduction in tutoring costs.

claim: This change prohibits a contributor from having several unrelated PRs open.
limits_and_alternatives: The qualifier defeats this broad reading; no claim is made about other unseen rules.

claim: Merged guidance permits maintainers to close trivial PRs or refactoring PRs with no clear benefit immediately.
limits_and_alternatives: May grants discretion; the text does not require closure or evidence an actual application in this PR.

claim: Merged guidance advises new contributors against submitting refactoring PRs.
limits_and_alternatives: Advisory should not is coded as recommendation; a stronger prohibition reading needs additional authority and usage evidence.

claim: A reviewer separately proposed closure when a refactoring PR attracts no reviewer; that wording is absent from the supplied final guide.
limits_and_alternatives: Absence was checked against the complete head file. A proposal in a merged thread is not automatically adopted.

claim: This PR demonstrates enforcement of the newly stated closure permission against an author.
limits_and_alternatives: The observed event revises guidance; an enforcement episode would need a separately linked application.

claim: The unmerged developer-notes proposal distinguishes conflict-driven rebasing from disruptive rebasing without conflicts and preserves within-branch fixups.
limits_and_alternatives: This is proposed wording in doc/developer-notes.md, not adopted CONTRIBUTING guidance.

claim: A suggestion to document DrahtBot warnings drew an objection about project and platform boundaries.
limits_and_alternatives: The participant assertion is not an independently verified organizational status of the bot.

claim: The record contains qualified support and a request to answer feedback despite eventual closure without merge.
limits_and_alternatives: Support, feedback and closure must remain separate events; positive review did not by itself establish integration.

claim: Closure establishes project-wide rejection of rebasing guidance or of the bot.
limits_and_alternatives: The packet does not establish a project-wide vote, unanimous judgment or a uniquely identified cause of closure.

claim: Standing guidance expects replies to review comments before merge, allows reasoned disagreement, and permits closure for inactive outstanding feedback.
limits_and_alternatives: The documented duty is to respond, not to accept every reviewer demand.

claim: maflcko explicitly links closure to alleged failures to prepare, explain and respond under the contribution guidelines.
limits_and_alternatives: This is an attributable enforcement claim with a provision, alleged trigger, actor and consequence. It does not independently establish every allegation or exclusive causation.

claim: The author disputes the technical criticism while agreeing to continue discussion in the issue.
limits_and_alternatives: Agreement to redirect discussion does not acknowledge all procedural allegations.

claim: The closure was caused solely by procedural noncompliance, independently of technical disagreement.
limits_and_alternatives: Participant reasoning supports a procedural mechanism; competing technical concerns and the counterfactual merge outcome remain unresolved.

claim: The contemporaneous guide specifies ACK with the top topic-branch commit followed by an account of the review.
limits_and_alternatives: A documented convention does not establish its enforcement in every review.

claim: practicalswift asks paymog to identify the reviewed version by adding its hash after ACK.
limits_and_alternatives: Local review coordination is explicit; no sanction is stated.

claim: paymog acknowledges the reminder and supplies a hash-specific ACK in a later comment.
limits_and_alternatives: The separate response supports local uptake. No population compliance rate or durable internalized belief follows.

claim: The body describes a software precondition, which supplies no institutional duty by itself.
limits_and_alternatives: Technical requires should not be converted to an institutional obligation without a separate governance claim.

claim: The author locally distinguishes a hash-specific code ACK from a concept ACK.
limits_and_alternatives: This combines a request and a classification claim; it does not make the author a unilateral rule maker.

claim: The stored bot table classifies purpleKarrot as stale and laanwj as ACK.
limits_and_alternatives: Mutable table contents have no reliable event time from their original creation timestamp.

claim: The merge message credits laanwj for the top commit and does not list purpleKarrot there.
limits_and_alternatives: Absence was checked against the full commit message. Attribution does not measure all influence on the contribution.

claim: Stale classification proves a reviewer was punished or excluded from deliberation.
limits_and_alternatives: Version-specific accounting and acknowledged input are a plausible alternative to punishment.

claim: A participant reports incorrect review classification and quotes an earlier table with vicjuma under Concept ACK.
limits_and_alternatives: This is a reported earlier state preserved by quotation, not an independently timestamped bot snapshot.

claim: The stored review already contains the final hash, while a later comment explains the missing-hash problem.
limits_and_alternatives: Review creation time precedes the reminder, but creation time is not edit time. The final stored text cannot resolve the update sequence.

claim: The recorded merge credits vicjuma and pablomartin4btc for the top commit.
limits_and_alternatives: This verifies final recorded attribution, not the exact earlier reclassification path.

claim: The reminder demonstrably caused an observed hash edit and bot update at their displayed creation times.
limits_and_alternatives: Edit history is absent. Preserve a plausible correction mechanism without assigning a fabricated time or causal effect.

claim: After merge, maflcko states a sufficiency threshold for relatively simple test PRs.
limits_and_alternatives: This is a scoped justification, not a universal mandatory threshold. The statement follows the recorded merge.

claim: promag challenges both review sufficiency and the handling of feedback.
limits_and_alternatives: A question can pragmatically challenge a decision; it does not establish the content of a settled general rule.

claim: A later reviewer proposes adding the missing explanation in a follow-up and receives acknowledgment.
limits_and_alternatives: Proposed follow-up is not verified implementation of that follow-up.

claim: Two untested ACKs or one tested ACK is an uncontested, project-wide merge requirement.
limits_and_alternatives: The assertion is conditional on simple test changes and contested locally. Courtesy afterward does not prove acceptance of the threshold.

claim: The proposed MAINTAINERS file sought to direct contributions toward maintained subsystems.
limits_and_alternatives: Its proposal status must remain separate from recognition of particular people and roles.

claim: The discussion contains a self-described mining role and explicit acknowledgment by another participant.
limits_and_alternatives: This supports local recognition, not an exhaustive or exclusive jurisdiction assignment.

claim: laanwj closes the inactive proposal while retaining support for the idea and inviting further work.
limits_and_alternatives: The stated reason includes workflow mismatch and inactivity; closure does not negate every role described.

claim: Failure to merge the maintainer document shows that subsystem roles did not exist.
limits_and_alternatives: Explicit local recognition coexists with failed codification; wider role arrangements remain unmeasured.

claim: The author presents the minimal MAINTAINERS proposal as descriptive documentation of existing practice.
limits_and_alternatives: The assertion of descriptiveness is an object of analysis, not proof every proposed sentence is true.

claim: Focus areas are debated as mutable descriptions; the author explicitly denies that they are enforced rules.
limits_and_alternatives: The local exchange weighs against reading listed areas as binding and exclusive jurisdiction.

claim: The author closes the unmerged proposal and leaves it available for others.
limits_and_alternatives: Author withdrawal is not a project-wide constitutional vote.

claim: The unmerged proposal establishes a newly adopted constitution allocating exclusive subsystem authority.
limits_and_alternatives: Discussion can concern recurring arrangements without establishing adoption, exclusivity or constitutional-level change.

claim: Several participants explicitly endorse achow101 for wallet maintenance, and an existing role holder identifies him as a replacement.
limits_and_alternatives: These are role endorsements; bare key checks elsewhere should not be pooled as identical endorsements.

claim: The merged repository adds the nominated key to the trusted-key list.
limits_and_alternatives: The technical signer list is observable; repository permission assignment and its time are not.

claim: The meeting left a decision open for comments; its suggested week of PR exposure exceeds the observed 3.46-day open-to-merge interval.
limits_and_alternatives: The waiting period was an expressed expectation with assent, not an established binding minimum. PR duration is not the length of the entire selection process.

claim: The key-list change proves the exact time of GitHub access assignment or confers authority over Bitcoin network adoption.
limits_and_alternatives: A repository verification artifact and bounded role endorsement do not observe either broader claim.

claim: The key holder proposes removal, and the merged change removes that key from the trusted list.
limits_and_alternatives: The frozen body author is laanwj. Removal from this list does not identify the timing of every other privilege change.

claim: Reviewers debate whether the proposed historical exceptions work, with later testing acknowledging a problem under disabled clean-merge checking.
limits_and_alternatives: Testing reports and agreement on intent do not show the full verification program is correct. The separate gate experiment tests a narrower mechanism.

claim: The original verification wrapper requires a matching trusted primary fingerprint for its valid-signature gate.
limits_and_alternatives: Twelve controlled executions with simulated GPG status confirm this gate only; no cryptographic or full-history verification is claimed.

claim: Removal establishes involuntary expulsion or a decision about ultimate governance legitimacy.
limits_and_alternatives: Self-initiation in the observed record and technical trust-list editing are insufficient for either conclusion.
